sections.title: (preamble)

notes.text: The Bachelor of Arts in Archaeology and Heritage Studies is an interdisciplinary major within the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences. Archaeology and heritage studies allow us to deepen our understanding of peoples and societies across space and time, in all parts of the world, while expanding our knowledge of issues relevant in contemporary society.
notes.source_line: The Bachelor of Arts in Archaeology and Heritage Studies is an interdisciplinary major within the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences. Archaeology and heritage studies allow us to deepen our understanding of peoples and societies across space and time, in all parts of the world, while expanding our knowledge of issues relevant in contemporary society.

notes.text: Students in this program gain tools to understand themselves and others in the past, present and future. Students may make discoveries in archaeology, engage in scientific analysis of ancient and contemporary materials, interpret the “stuff” and stories we live with and use to define ourselves at all scales from family to nation; work to preserve historical places, or create unforgettable exhibits in museums or experiences in virtual spaces.
notes.source_line: Students in this program gain tools to understand themselves and others in the past, present and future. Students may make discoveries in archaeology, engage in scientific analysis of ancient and contemporary materials, interpret the “stuff” and stories we live with and use to define ourselves at all scales from family to nation; work to preserve historical places, or create unforgettable exhibits in museums or experiences in virtual spaces.

notes.text: The BA in Archaeology and Heritage Studies enhances students’ preparation for a wide range of professional careers and/or graduate study through an emphasis on experiential learning, principled debate, and consideration of what matters and why in society today and long ago. Majors strengthen their skills in critical thinking by gathering and assessing evidence and formulating clear and persuasive arguments, both oral and written. Additionally, students gain an understanding of the compliance and policy environments that promote attention to heritage in all forms, locally, nationally, and globally.

Majors strengthen their skills in critical thinking by gathering and assessing evidence and formulating clear and persuasive arguments, both oral and written. Additionally, students gain an understanding of the compliance and policy environments that promote attention to heritage in all forms, locally, nationally, and globally.

notes.text: Students from a wide range of disciplines gain valuable perspectives applicable to their intellectual and professional interests through the study of archaeology and heritage studies.

notes.text: This compact, flexible BA program allows students to craft a path that is appropriate for their interests and enables students to explore minors or other programs at USC so that they are broadly prepared for success.
notes.source_line: This compact, flexible BA program allows students to craft a path that is appropriate for their interests and enables students to explore minors or other programs at USC so that they are broadly prepared for success.

notes.text: In addition to a wide choice of elective courses, students fulfill six requirements in this 36-unit BA program. The lower-division foundation course is ANTH 202 Archaeology: Our Human Past. Students choose electives from a list, and this includes one upper-division course that enables exploration of theoretical approaches; at least one upper-division course that supports experiential, practicum, or research; one ethics and heritage class; and a capstone course that provides exposure to the debates surrounding heritage and archaeology in contemporary society.
